heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P requires an upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle and extruder gears before safely processing abrasive Polymaker PA6-CF, which is speed-capped at 131 mm/s due to an 11 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. While small functional parts can be printed without an enclosure at a 45°C bed temp, larger structural prints necessitate an enclosure or draft shield to mitigate severe warping.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate or Engineering Plate with Magigoo PA or PVA glue stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 11 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap print speed automatically at 131 mm/s for a 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width.
Disable the auxiliary part cooling fan completely and set the part cooling fan threshold to 0% min and 20% max to preserve layer adhesion and prevent warping on the open-frame P1P.
Enable a 5mm outer brim with a 0.0mm brim-object gap to aggressively anchor corner edges to the build plate during cool-down.
Set the nozzle temperature to 290°C and bed temperature to 45°C, ensuring the 'Keep fan always on' checkbox is unchecked.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe corner lifting and delamination from build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Ambient drafts cooling the nylon unevenly on the open-frame P1P, combined with high thermal contraction of PA6.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply Magigoo PA on the build plate, add an external draft shield or enclosure cover, and increase brim width to 8mm with zero offset.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough, matte surface with popping sounds and severe stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption; PA6 is intensely hygroscopic and saturates within hours of exposure to ambient air.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated convection dryer at 80-100°C for 8 to 12 hours and print directly from an active dry box.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rapid nozzle orifice expansion and extrusion inconsistency
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Using the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle, which is rapidly eroded by the abrasive chopped carbon fibers.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Swap the stock hotend assembly for an official Bambu Lab 0.4mm or 0.6mm Hardened Steel Hotend and hardened steel extruder gear assembly.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PA6-CF on a stock P1P without modifications?
faq.answer: No. The stock P1P uses a stainless steel nozzle and unhardened extruder gears which will rapidly wear out from the abrasive carbon fibers; you must upgrade both to hardened steel components.

faq.question: Does the open-frame P1P require an enclosure to print this filament?
faq.answer: Polymaker PA6-CF prints at a low bed temperature of 40-50°C to minimize crystallization shrinkage, allowing small parts to print openly; however, medium-to-large prints will warp significantly without an enclosure or draft protection.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu AMS to feed Polymaker PA6-CF?
faq.answer: Yes, but prolonged use of abrasive CF filament through the plastic AMS funnels will cause grooving; installing hardened PTFE funnel guides or printing directly from an external dry box is recommended.

faq.question: Why is the recommended bed temperature only 45°C for a high-temp nylon?
faq.answer: Polymaker formulates their PA6-CF with specialized crystallization kinetics where lower bed temperatures (40-50°C) prevent premature stress buildup and warping that typically occur at higher bed temps.
